standard_prerequisites.name: Adding a free direct summand preserves freeness, and direct sums of free modules are free
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 79, 84-87 and 88-89 when the free modules R^{n+m}, R^m and R^n are assembled
standard_prerequisites.use: Realizes the stable isomorphism explicitly: it is what lets a module M with M + R^n free be recognised as stably free, and it is applied under the regrouping of the direct sum in the second case.

core_obligations: Split the sequence by projectivity to fix an isomorphism P = P' + P'' and reduce the hypothesis 'two out of three stably free' to three cases, of which the proof treats two explicitly and obtains the third by symmetry (proof lines 77-78 and 88-89).
Case P' and P'' stably free: from P' + R^n free and P'' + R^m free, show that P + R^{n+m} is free by distributing the two free summands over the split decomposition of P (proof lines 78-80).

Case P' and P' stably free: reorganise the direct sum P'' + (P' + R^m) + R^n, which is free because it equals (P + R^n) + R^m, so that P'' shows up as the complement of a free direct summand; this is the one case in which the stably free conclusions have to be shuffled between the terms (proof lines 80-88).
Conclude that the third module is stably free in the remaining case by invoking symmetry of the two cases just handled (proof lines 88-89).
proof_roadmap: Because the modules are projective, the short exact sequence splits, giving P = P' + P'' (proof lines 77-78).
First case: if P' + R^n and P'' + R^m are free, then P + R^{n+m} = (P' + R^n) + (P'' + R^m) is free, so P is stably free (proof lines 78-80).

Second case: if P + R^n and P' + R^m are free, form P'' + (P' + R^m) + R^n, rewrite it as (P'' + P') + R^m + R^n = (P + R^n) + R^m, which is free, and read the stable freeness of P'' off that identity (proof lines 80-88).
Third case: obtained from the second by symmetry (proof lines 88-89).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a 2-out-of-3 statement for stably free modules over an arbitrary ring, inside a short exact sequence of finite projective modules, and its proof has to treat the three possible selections of the two stably free terms (statement lines 71-73). The case where the middle term P and the submodule P' are the stably free ones is the non-formal one: one has to display P'' as the complement of a free direct summand by rewriting P'' + (P' + R^m) + R^n in two different groupings and using the given freeness of P + R^n, rather than by cancelling free summands (proof lines 80-88). The remaining case is then dismissed by symmetry. The proof uses only that the sequence of projectives splits and the definition of stable freeness, both of which stay outside the counted span as standard prerequisites.
